items.title: Hackers Are Using Real Dell and Staples Emails to Make Their Scams Look Legitimate
items.description: Hackers are abusing genuine Dell and Staples order emails to make fake purchase alerts look credible. Instead of sending a forged message, they place scam instructions inside order details that trusted retail systems deliver, pushing recipients toward phone numbers controlled by the attackers. items.description: China-state-aligned hackers used ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration-testing framework, to attempt access to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants following the ConnectWise Cloud Backup breach. items.title: GoDaddy Revoking 404,607 TLS Certificates Following Compliance Failures
items.description: GoDaddy launched a mass revocation of 404,607 SSL/TLS certificates after finding that issued certificates did not match its published certificate policies. items.title: Node.js Releases Security Updates to Fix High-Severity TLS, DNS, and Brotli Vulnerabilities
items.description: Node.js has released security updates for its 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x branches to address ten vulnerabilities, including four high-severity flaws affecting DNS lookups, TLS certificate checks, and Brotli decompression. The supplied release details identify 26.12.1, 24.22.1, and 22.23.4 as the patched versions. The most serious potential outcome is remote code execution through the Brotli decoder.…
